Chapter 15: The Invitation to Wonder
Have you ever felt like there’s a bit of magic hidden in the everyday world—just waiting for you to notice? That’s exactly the feeling Emily Dickinson’s poems invite us to explore. Her writing gently nudges us to look closer, to ask questions, and to let our sense of wonder guide us through life.
Imagine a child lying in the grass, gazing up as clouds drift lazily across the sky. Every shape tells a story. Every slow shift is a little mystery. Dickinson’s poems capture that exact sense of possibility—the way curiosity can turn something ordinary into something extraordinary. And here’s the thing: wonder isn’t just for kids. It’s for anyone who’s willing to see the world with fresh eyes.
But let’s be real—most of us lose touch with that spark as we get older. Life gets busy. Responsibilities pile up. Routine takes over. Still, these poems quietly remind us: wonder is a choice. It’s a way of moving through the world—staying open, curious, and fully alive. Sometimes the greatest discoveries are hiding just beyond what we already know.
Picture this: someone standing out in the rain, feeling the drops soak into their skin. There’s nothing complicated about it, but it’s profound all the same—a reminder of what it’s like to be truly present, to sense the world’s endless surprises. Dickinson’s poems linger right there, in that simple joy of being alive and letting go of certainty so you can embrace the unknown.
Of course, wonder isn’t always easy. It makes us vulnerable. There’s the risk of disappointment, or the fear of looking silly. But that’s just part of the deal. To really experience wonder, you need a little courage—a willingness to be surprised, to maybe even be changed.
So, as the child in the grass finally closes their eyes, there’s a deep sense of peace. The world might be vast and mysterious, but it’s also quietly welcoming. Dickinson’s poems offer us a fresh way to see life—as an adventure, full of hidden joys for those who pay attention. In the end, they become companions for any of us who’ve ever longed for a bit of magic, or found ourselves wondering what else might be possible.
